title: Whether US tariffs on Singapore are pushing up prices for lower-income households
asked: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked what criteria the Ministry of Trade and Industry uses to decide when US tariff impacts turn into price pressures for everyday Singaporeans, especially lower-income households, and how often those criteria are reviewed.
response: Ms Gan Siow Huang said Singapore's exports to the US face a baseline reciprocal tariff of 10%, plus Section 232 sectoral tariffs such as on steel and aluminium, and that non-oil domestic exports to the US fell 9.2% year-on-year from April to December 2025. She said the tariffs and the export decline are not expected to directly affect Singapore's inflation because US importers pay the tariffs, though higher US prices could indirectly raise prices of US exports, including to Singapore, in future. So far no tariff impact on Singapore's import prices has been observed, and falling import prices helped bring CPI-All Items inflation to 0.9% and MAS Core Inflation to 0.7% last year. She said the ministry will keep monitoring import prices, inflation and the impact on Singaporeans, especially lower-income households, and stands ready to provide further support if needed.

key_points.point: Singapore's exports to the US face a baseline reciprocal tariff of 10%, with additional Section 232 sectoral tariffs such as on steel and aluminium.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: Singapore's exports to the United States (US) are currently subject to a baseline "reciprocal" tariff rate of 10%.

key_points.point: Non-oil domestic exports to the US fell 9.2% year-on-year from April to December 2025.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: Singapore's non-oil domestic exports to the US fell by 9.2% year-on-year from April to December 2025.

key_points.point: The tariffs and export decline are not expected to directly affect Singapore's inflation because US importers pay the tariffs.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: The tariffs and corresponding decline in exports to the US are not expected to have a direct impact on Singapore's inflation.

key_points.point: An indirect effect is possible if higher US prices raise the prices of US exports, including to Singapore, in future.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: there could be an indirect impact if higher prices in the US lead to an increase in the prices of its exports, including to Singapore, in the future

key_points.point: No tariff impact on Singapore's import prices has been observed so far, with import prices falling in 2025.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: we have not observed any tariff impact on Singapore's import prices, with our import prices falling in 2025

key_points.point: Falling import prices helped lower CPI-All Items inflation to 0.9% and MAS Core Inflation to 0.7% last year.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: the decline in import prices helped to lower Consumer Price Index (CPI)-All Items inflation and Monetary Authority of Singapore's Core Inflation to 0.9% and 0.7% respectively last year

key_points.point: The ministry will keep monitoring import prices, inflation and the impact on Singaporeans, especially lower-income households, and is ready to give further support if needed.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: we stand ready to provide further support if needed

key_points.point: The ministry looks at various indices and indicators to understand inflation's impact on different household income groups.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: we do look at various indices and indicators to understand the impact of inflation on different household income groups

key_points.point: CPI-All Items inflation for the lowest 20% income household group was 0.6% last year.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: for the lowest 20% income household groups, we know that last year the CPI-All Items inflation for them was 0.6%

key_points.point: That compares with 0.9% for the middle 60% income group.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: this is different from that for the middle 60% income group of 0.9%

left_open: How often the criteria for assessing tariff-driven price pressures are reviewed
The specific criteria used to determine when tariff impacts translate into price pressures for everyday Singaporeans
supplementary: Whether the ministry uses indicators to spot disproportionate inflation effects on lower-income households, such as basic food, transport and utilities costs.
